action.rationale: A 26-year-old woman presented with ~3 months of sicca symptoms (dry mouth, dry eyes, vaginal dryness, thirst) plus painful, antibiotic-refractory bilateral submandibular gland enlargement and 10 kg weight loss. Objective dryness was confirmed (Schirmer's 4–5 mm; unstimulated salivary flow 0.04 mL/min) and ultrasound showed bilaterally enlarged, hypoechoic, heterogeneous submandibular glands. Laboratory findings supportive of an IgG4-related systemic process included elevated ESR (62 mm/h), a positive ANA (1:160), hypocomplementemia (C3 81, C4 11), and elevated serum IgE (210 IU/mL) with an atopic family history; infection was excluded (negative HIV, HCV, cryoglobulins; sterile bacterial/mycobacterial/fungal cultures and stains). The decisive finding was submandibular gland biopsy showing a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with reactive lymphoid follicular hyperplasia, acinar atrophy and interstitial fibrosis, and 19 IgG4-positive plasma cells/HPF with an IgG4:IgG ratio >0.5 and a polytypic plasma cell population without granulomas or malignancy. A labial salivary gland biopsy showed a focus score of 0 with no lymphoepithelial lesions, arguing against Sjögren's syndrome, and the absence of granulomas, organisms, and clonal lymphocytes excludes sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, and lymphoma. This constellation fulfills the clinical, serologic, radiologic, and histopathologic features of IgG4-related disease presenting as IgG4-related sialadenitis (Mikulicz disease).

final.rationale: A 26-year-old woman presented with ~3 months of sicca symptoms (dry mouth, dry eyes, vaginal dryness, thirst) plus painful, antibiotic-refractory bilateral submandibular gland enlargement and 10 kg weight loss. Objective dryness was confirmed (Schirmer's 4–5 mm; unstimulated salivary flow 0.04 mL/min) and ultrasound showed bilaterally enlarged, hypoechoic, heterogeneous submandibular glands. Laboratory findings supportive of an IgG4-related systemic process included elevated ESR (62 mm/h), a positive ANA (1:160), hypocomplementemia (C3 81, C4 11), and elevated serum IgE (210 IU/mL) with an atopic family history; infection was excluded (negative HIV, HCV, cryoglobulins; sterile bacterial/mycobacterial/fungal cultures and stains). The decisive finding was submandibular gland biopsy showing a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with reactive lymphoid follicular hyperplasia, acinar atrophy and interstitial fibrosis, and 19 IgG4-positive plasma cells/HPF with an IgG4:IgG ratio >0.5 and a polytypic plasma cell population without granulomas or malignancy. A labial salivary gland biopsy showed a focus score of 0 with no lymphoepithelial lesions, arguing against Sjögren's syndrome, and the absence of granulomas, organisms, and clonal lymphocytes excludes sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, and lymphoma. This constellation fulfills the clinical, serologic, radiologic, and histopathologic features of IgG4-related disease presenting as IgG4-related sialadenitis (Mikulicz disease).

judgement.rationale: The candidate identifies IgG4-related sialadenitis, which is the same core disease and anatomic site as IgG4-associated chronic sclerosing sialadenitis/Kuttner tumor; the broader IgG4-related disease label and Mikulicz disease alternative are directly related and do not introduce an unrelated or wrong diagnosis.
